title: WHERE THE HAIL DID NOT FALL

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Throughout Egypt hail struck everything in the fields—both people and animals; it beat down everything growing in the fields and stripped every tree. The only place it did not hail was the land of Goshen, where the Israelites were." - Exodus 9:25-26 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Everything stripped, everything beaten down — except Goshen.

We should not read this as a promise that Christians will always be spared trouble. Scripture is clear that we are not exempt from suffering. Believers were in the Colosseum. Believers were in the concentration camps. Believers are in hospital wards today. Jesus promised His followers trouble in this world, not immunity from it (Jn 16:33).

So what is Goshen telling us? It is telling us that God is able to distinguish, that His people are never lost in the crowd, and that no judgement falls on them by accident.

There is a Goshen for every believer, though it is not a postcode. It is a position. Paul says nothing in all creation can separate us from the love of God in Christ Jesus (Rom 8:38-39). Storms may reach us. Condemnation cannot.

The hail fell on all Egypt. It did not fall on Goshen. And the judgement we deserved fell on Christ, not on us.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Am I looking for a Goshen of circumstances rather than resting in Christ?
2. What difference does it make that judgement fell on Jesus instead of me?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord Jesus, thank You for taking the storm that should have fallen on me. Keep me secure in You whatever the weather. Amen.
